items.title: Kyiv and Moscow trade attacks as peace talks are pencilled in for November
items.summary: Al Jazeera's Russia page and a search summary of recent reports say overnight attacks on Kyiv injured 15 people, Russia said it intercepted 163 drones, and Ukraine reported strikes on a plant in Yelets on 25 and 26 October. Reports also say Russia and Ukraine have talks planned for November in the UAE. Casualty and loss figures come from the warring parties and are provisional.
items.why: Talks, sanctions easing and energy prices feed straight into global hiring budgets and consumer demand that employers plan around.

items.title: US-Iran talks stall; Trump says no attack before the 3 November midterms
items.summary: CBS News' live coverage and a search summary report that Trump said last Thursday (22 October) the US will not attack Iran before the 3 November congressional midterms, while Iran has set red lines for talks and Russia's Lavrov visited Tehran. Details move fast and come from several outlets, so treat them as provisional.
items.why: A Gulf conflict moves oil prices and investor risk appetite, which shape company hiring and marketing spend.

items.title: Jio Platforms refunds due today, listing set for 28 October
items.summary: HDFC Sky and India TV report that the Rs 30,213 crore Jio Platforms issue priced at Rs 1,119 closed about 22.2 times subscribed, with allotment on 26 October, refunds and share credit on 27 October and listing on BSE and NSE on 28 October. One report puts the unofficial grey-market premium near Rs 249, which is indicative only and not a guarantee of the listing price.
items.why: India's largest IPO shows how markets price subscriber scale and brand strength, a useful lens for marketing strategy.

items.title: Sensex and Nifty snap a four-session losing run on 26 October
items.summary: BusinessToday reports that the Sensex and Nifty ended Monday's session higher after four straight falls, recovering from intraday lows to gain over 1 per cent each according to one market summary. The exact closing levels differ between sources and are provisional.
items.why: Market swings change campus-hiring sentiment and the risk appetite of the companies recruiting this season.

items.title: Nvidia unveils OpenShell architecture for governed AI agents
items.summary: AI Weekly's digest lists Nvidia's OpenShell reference architecture for governed AI agents, announced on 21 October at GTC Berlin, and the open Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B model released on 23 October. These are company announcements and have not been independently tested.
items.why: Governance for AI agents is becoming a selling point and a hiring need in HR, risk and marketing roles.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly weighs a software fee of $2,000 per GPU
items.summary: AI Weekly reports that Nvidia is considering an annual fee of $2,000 per GPU for software that runs agents on AI factories; this is a report, not an announced price.
items.why: Pricing models for AI software decide who captures value, a classic marketing question.
